question.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 4-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ -\lambda |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ -\lambda [(1-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-4)] & =0 \\ -\lambda ({\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda +4-4) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}(\lambda -5) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =5,\,0,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{5} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{0}=0 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$
